question: Your customer support agent's system prompt instructs it to verify the customer's identity with get_customer before it calls process_refund. Production logs show that in about 2% of conversations, the agent calls process_refund without a verified customer ID. Company policy requires this verification before every financial operation, without exception. Which change best addresses this problem?

options.text: Instruct the agent to state in its reply that it verified the customer before it describes any refund to the customer.
options.reason: This is another prompt instruction with a non-zero failure rate. It also does nothing to block process_refund when verification has not happened.

options.text: Rewrite the system prompt so the verification rule appears first, in capital letters, and is repeated before each tool description.
options.reason: Stronger wording is still prompt-based guidance. The guide states that prompt instructions alone keep a non-zero failure rate when deterministic compliance is required.

options.text: Add few-shot examples to the system prompt that show the agent calling get_customer before every process_refund call.
options.reason: Few-shot examples are still prompt-based guidance. They can lower the failure rate, but they cannot guarantee the required ordering the way a programmatic gate can.

options.text: Add a hook that intercepts each process_refund call and blocks it until get_customer has returned a verified customer ID.
options.reason: The policy requires deterministic compliance, and prompt instructions alone have a non-zero failure rate. A programmatic prerequisite blocks the downstream call every time.
